validation.notes: Repair: packages/agent/src/harness/runtime/drive/tools.ts, recoverToolInvocation. Replay is now gated on the current declaration as well as the persisted intent: `if (tool !== undefined && !cancelled && call.replay === "safe" && tool.replay === "safe")`. A persisted-safe call whose tool is now missing, no longer declares a policy, or downgraded to "never" settles through the existing readCheckpoint -> interruptedOutcome -> publishToolOutcome path (durable checkpoint text plus the interruption marker, isError true) instead of clearing the checkpoint and re-executing the effect; a still-present, still-safe, non-cancelled call keeps replaying with its persisted arguments. Regression: .prale-eval/regression.mjs drives the real recoverToolInvocation via .prale-eval/subject.mjs (createRecoverySubject), asserting exact boundary event sequences (["read","publish"] vs ["clear","invoke","effect-complete","publish"]), zero effect executions, published outcome shape (toolCall id, role, isError, terminate, checkpoint content/details preserved, marker text), and the unchanged replay path. Cases: (1) declared safe -> never, (2) tool missing, (3) tool without a policy, (4) persisted never / declared safe, (5) both safe but cancelled, (6) both safe and live replays once with persisted args. Evidence: on the pristine baseline source (git checkout of packages/agent/src/harness/runtime/drive/tools.ts) the script exits 1 with AssertionError 'changed declaration: the tool effect must not run: 1 !== 0'; with the repair applied it exits 0 with 'recovery replay policy regression: all assertions passed'. A partially-correct variant that only guards tool presence also fails the same assertion. Limitation: node_modules is absent, so the repo's vitest suite and tsc/tsgo typecheck could not be run; validation used only the Node 24 runtime (v24.14.0) with --experimental-vm-modules, which emitted only experimental-feature warnings.
